scope: post-outcome MaleCNS development mechanism; not biological/population/sex confirmation

subspace_geometry.finding: BM cut effects are strongly low-dimensional in both Real and null systems.
subspace_geometry.limit: Low dimensionality itself is not Real-specific.

reciprocity_matched_null.finding: Exact reciprocal-degree preservation leaves most of the Male Real-null gap.
reciprocity_matched_null.limit: Reciprocity quantity is insufficient; partner placement remains implicated.

fixed_support_weight_null.finding: Real support retains a majority of Male gain while source-local weights add a substantial component.
fixed_support_weight_null.limit: Topology and weight are not independent biological replicates.

topology_weight_factorial.finding: Weight effects are consistently positive on Real support and approximately absent on rewired support.
topology_weight_factorial.limit: This is a within-graph counterfactual interaction.

edge_class_weight.finding: Reciprocal and unidirectional weight sensitivity differs between Male and Female development panels.
edge_class_weight.limit: No common edge-class mechanism or sex inference is supported.

class_allocation.finding: Per-source reciprocal/unidirectional class allocation reproduces most of the Male full weight-shuffle effect.

preserved_negative_results: The original common two-system biological-specificity gate failed.
Fresh-cue generalization did not establish a common biological advantage.
No single outlet or individual edge explains the effect.
Low-dimensional BM geometry is shared by Real and null systems.
Reciprocity count and per-node reciprocal degree do not explain the Male effect.
A common Male/Female reciprocal-edge mechanism was not found.
next_valid_test: Outcome-blind replication of the frozen chain in an independent connectome specimen; a new version of the same specimen is technical robustness only.
